title: Momentum Transfer Lab: Collision Dynamics
description: A physics sandbox where a ShaderBall and Corset sit on a frictionless rail system. The user configures mass, velocity, and elasticity for each object, launches collisions, observes momentum and kinetic energy conservation in real-time graphs, and can undo/redo parameter changes to compare outcomes.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a 1D collision physics lab. Load ShaderBall.glb and Corset.glb using GLTFLoader. Normalize both models to roughly 1 unit bounding box and place them on a visible rail (a long thin box) at x=-4 and x=4 respectively, resting on a ground plane with grid. Use OrbitControls for camera, starting at position (0,3,10) looking at origin. Add hemisphere light plus directional light with soft shadows enabled on a MeshStandardMaterial ground.

Create an HTML/CSS overlay panel with: (1) mass sliders for each object (0.5-10 kg), (2) initial velocity sliders for each object (-10 to 10 m/s, ShaderBall defaults positive, Corset defaults negative), (3) a coefficient-of-restitution slider (0=perfectly inelastic to 1=perfectly elastic), (4) a Launch button, (5) a Reset button, (6) Undo and Redo buttons for parameter changes. Store parameter history in an array with a pointer index for undo/redo (minimum 10 states deep).

On Launch, animate both objects sliding along the rail toward each other at their set velocities. Detect collision when bounding boxes overlap. Compute post-collision velocities using the 1D collision formula with the restitution coefficient. Display a real-time overlay showing: total momentum (should remain constant, shown as a horizontal bar), total kinetic energy (bar that changes for inelastic collisions), and individual velocity vectors as colored arrows above each object using ArrowHelper. After collision, objects continue at new velocities until they leave the rail bounds.

Show a live 2D canvas graph (bottom-right corner, 250x150px) plotting total momentum and total kinetic energy over time during the animation. Color-code momentum in blue and energy in red. After each run, the user can adjust parameters (each change is tracked for undo/redo), then relaunch. The Reset button returns objects to starting positions. Add subtle particle burst effect at collision point using a BufferGeometry point cloud. All interactions must total 10-14 steps for a full experiment cycle: adjust 2 masses, 2 velocities, restitution, launch, observe, reset, undo a parameter, redo it, relaunch with new elasticity, compare energy graphs.
